The Golden Eagles, led by fourth-year head coach [[Shaka Smart]], played their home games at [[Fiserv Forum]] in [[Milwaukee|Milwaukee, Wisconsin]] as a member of the [[Big East Conference]]. The Marquette Golden Eagles drew an average home attendance of 15,571, the 9th highest of all college basketball teams.https://stats.ncaa.org/rankings/change_sport_year_div ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Golden Eagles]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 27–10, 14–6 in Big East play to finish in tie for second place. As a No. 3 seed in the [[2024 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they defeated [[2023–24 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball season|Villanova]] in the quarterfinals and [[2023–24 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the semifinals to advance to the championship game, where they lost to [[2023–24 UConn Huskies men's basketball season|UConn]].{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/villanova-basketball-marquette-big-east-tournament-score-ncaa-20240315.html|title=Villanova bows out of Big East Tournament in overtime loss to Marquette, likely ending NCAA hopes|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|first=Jeff|last=Neiburg|date=March 15, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2024/03/15/providence-loses-to-marquette-79-68-in-big-east-tournament/72987880007/|title=Providence basketball falls to Marquette in Big East semifinals. Will Friars reach Big Dance?|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|first=Bill|last=Koch|date=March 15, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/big-east-tournament-donovan-clingan-huskies-19127770.php|title=UConn men's basketball team wins Big East Tournament title with win over Marquette: 'Feels special'|work=[[CT Insider]]|first=David|last=Borges|date=March 16, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the South region.
